name: JNVST Class 6
fullName: Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Selection Test – Class VI
conductingBody: Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), Ministry of Education
approxCandidates: ≈30 lakh registrations a year for about 49,000 Class 6 seats in 650+ JNVs
eligibility: Studying in Class 5 in 2026-27 in a recognised school of the same district; born 1 May 2015 – 31 Jul 2017 (for JNVST 2027); 75% seats for rural candidates; one attempt only

notification.summary: JNVST 2027 (admission session 2027-28) registration opened in early July 2026 and, after extensions, closed on 10 Aug 2026 (correction window 11–12 Aug). The test is scheduled in a single phase on Saturday, 28 Nov 2026, 11:30 AM – 1:30 PM. Admit cards are expected about 3–4 weeks before the exam and results around March 2027.

pattern.notes: Each question carries 1.25 marks and there is no negative marking. 10 extra minutes are given to read instructions. The real Mental Ability section is entirely figure-based (10 parts × 4 questions). Because this mock is text-only, the figure questions are replaced by text equivalents (letter/number patterns, described folds and mirrors, cube/dice facts) that test the same skills. The Language test uses 4 passages × 5 questions; here passages are repeated inside each question.

trendAnalysis.summary: Based on the 2024 paper and the two-phase 2025 and 2026 tests. The pattern has been fixed since 2020: Mental Ability (50%) decides the merit, with odd-one-out, figure series, mirror imaging, punched-hole and embedded-figure items of easy to moderate level. Arithmetic covers the Class 5 syllabus, with number system, fractions/decimals, measurement, percentage/profit-loss and area-perimeter being the high-yield topics; recent papers favour short word problems over plain computation. The Language test has four easy factual passages, with occasional vocabulary-in-context and title questions. Overall difficulty is easy to moderate; speed and accuracy in Mental Ability matter most.

resources.notes: NVS publishes the prospectus with sample questions (linked as officialMock) for each section on navodaya.gov.in. Answer keys and question papers are not released officially; past papers circulate through publishers. Results are published district-wise on navodaya.gov.in and the CBSE ITMS portal (cbseitms.rcil.gov.in).

questions.question: Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Apple, mango and banana are fruits; potato is a vegetable (an underground stem).

questions.question: Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: 4, 8 and 12 are even numbers (and multiples of 4); 15 is odd.

questions.question: Find the odd letter-pair out.
questions.explanation: AB, CD and EF are pairs of consecutive letters; in GI the letter H is skipped.

questions.question: Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Circle, square and triangle are flat (2-D) figures; a cube is a solid (3-D) figure.

questions.question: What comes next in the series: 1, 4, 9, 16, ?
questions.explanation: These are squares: 1², 2², 3², 4², so the next term is 5² = 25.

questions.question: What comes next in the series: Z, X, V, T, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter goes two steps back in the alphabet: T − 2 = R.

questions.question: What comes next in the series: AZ, BY, CX, ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) and the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W): DW.

questions.question: A series of shapes is: triangle, square, pentagon, ? Which shape comes next?
questions.explanation: The number of sides increases by one each time: 3, 4, 5, so the next shape has 6 sides – a hexagon.

questions.question: An arrow points North. In each step of a figure series it turns 90° clockwise. In which direction does it point after 3 steps?
questions.explanation: North → East (1) → South (2) → West (3).

questions.question: What comes next in the series: 5, 10, 20, 40, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is double the previous one: 40 × 2 = 80.

questions.question: Bird : Nest :: Bee : ?
questions.explanation: A bird lives in a nest; a bee lives in a hive. A den is for a lion, a burrow for a rabbit and a stable for a horse.

questions.question: Square : 4 :: Triangle : ?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 sides; a triangle has 3 sides.

questions.question: ACE : BDF :: GIK : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter of ACE moves one step forward to make BDF. So G→H, I→J, K→L gives HJL.

questions.question: The small letter 'b' is seen in a mirror placed upright to its right. How does its mirror image look?
questions.explanation: An upright (vertical) mirror swaps left and right but keeps up and down. The bowl of 'b' moves from the right side to the left, so it looks like 'd'.

questions.question: Which of these capital letters looks exactly the same in an upright mirror placed beside it?
questions.explanation: An upright mirror reverses left and right. 'A' has a vertical line of symmetry, so it looks the same. B, E and K are symmetric only about a horizontal line, so they look reversed.

questions.question: A wall clock without numbers is seen in a mirror and appears to show 3:00. What is the actual time?
questions.explanation: For a mirror image of a clock, actual time = 12:00 − time shown = 12:00 − 3:00 = 9:00. (At 9:00 the hour hand points left; in the mirror it appears to point right, like 3:00.)

questions.question: The word TOM is written on a card and seen in an upright mirror placed beside it. Since T, O and M are each symmetric about a vertical line, what does the image read?
questions.explanation: An upright mirror reverses the order of letters; because T, O and M look the same when flipped, the image reads MOT.

questions.question: Which option is exactly the same as BD8QP6?
questions.explanation: Only BD8QP6 matches every character in the same order; the others swap P/Q, B/D or 8/6.

questions.question: Which option is exactly the same as MN5W2V?
questions.explanation: Compare character by character: only MN5W2V matches. The others swap M/N, W/V or 5/2.

questions.question: Find the missing number in this pattern. Row 1: 2, 4, 8. Row 2: 3, 6, 12. Row 3: 5, 10, ?
questions.explanation: In each row every number is double the one before it: 10 × 2 = 20.

questions.question: Find the missing number. Row 1: 3, 4, 7. Row 2: 5, 2, 7. Row 3: 6, ?, 7
questions.explanation: In each row, first number + second number = third number: 6 + 1 = 7.

questions.question: Two identical right-angled isosceles triangles are joined along their longest sides. Which figure is formed?
questions.explanation: Joining two equal isosceles right triangles along the hypotenuse gives four equal sides and four right angles – a square.

questions.question: Into how many equal parts do the two diagonals of a square divide it?
questions.explanation: The two diagonals cross at the centre and make 4 equal triangles.

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded once in half, and one hole is punched through both layers. How many holes will there be when the sheet is unfolded?
questions.explanation: The punch goes through 2 layers, so 2 holes appear, placed symmetrically about the fold line.

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded in half and then folded in half again. One hole is punched through all the layers. How many holes will there be when it is fully unfolded?
questions.explanation: Two folds make 4 layers, so one punch makes 4 holes.

questions.question: On a standard dice, the numbers on opposite faces always add up to 7. Which number is opposite the face showing 2?
questions.explanation: 2 + 5 = 7, so 5 is opposite 2.

questions.question: A wooden cube painted on all its faces is cut into 27 equal smaller cubes. How many small cubes have no paint on any face?
questions.explanation: A 3 × 3 × 3 cube has only one cube hidden in the centre: (3 − 2)³ = 1.

questions.question: Which of these words is hidden (letters together, in the same order) in the word CATERPILLAR?
questions.explanation: CATER-PILLAR contains PILLAR as a continuous part. The other words do not appear as continuous letters.

questions.question: In which of these words is the word ANT hidden (letters together, in the same order)?
questions.explanation: PL-ANT contains 'ANT'. PAINT has 'AINT', TAN has the letters in a different order, and NEAT does not contain it.

questions.question: What is the place value of 7 in 47,325?
questions.explanation: 7 is in the thousands place, so its place value is 7 × 1000 = 7,000.

questions.question: Which number does the Roman numeral XLIV stand for?
questions.explanation: XL = 40 and IV = 4, so XLIV = 44.

questions.question: What is the LCM of 4, 6 and 8?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24 … 24 is the first one divisible by both 4 and 6.

questions.question: What is the HCF of 36 and 48?
questions.explanation: 36 = 12 × 3 and 48 = 12 × 4, and 3 and 4 have no common factor, so the HCF is 12.
25 × 4 = 100; there are 3 decimal places in total, so the answer is 0.100 = 0.1.

questions.question: What is 25% of 360?
A toy bought for ₹250 is sold for ₹300. What is the profit per cent?
What is the simple interest on ₹800 at 5% per year for 3 years?
A car travels at 60 km per hour. How far will it go in 2½ hours?
questions.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

questions.question: 3 km 250 m is equal to how many metres?
How many minutes are there in 2½ hours?
questions.explanation: 2 hours = 120 minutes and ½ hour = 30 minutes; total 150 minutes.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a square of side 9 cm?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 4 × side = 4 × 9 = 36 cm.

questions.question: What is the area of a rectangular field 15 m long and 8 m wide?
questions.explanation: Area = length × breadth = 15 × 8 = 120 m².

questions.question: What is the measure of each angle of an equilateral triangle?
questions.explanation: All three angles are equal and add up to 180°, so each is 60°.

Passage: Sundarpur was a small village with a big pond at its centre. Every summer the pond dried up, and the women had to walk three kilometres to fetch water. One year, the school teacher, Mr. Rao, asked the children to help. Together with their parents, they cleaned the pond, removed the plastic waste and dug small channels so that rainwater from the fields would flow into it. When the monsoon came, the pond filled to the brim. By the next summer there was still water in it, and the women no longer had to walk far. The villagers decided to celebrate 'Pond Day' every year.

Question: Why did the women have to walk three kilometres in summer?
options: Because the pond was very dirty
Because they wanted to meet friends
Because the teacher told them to
questions.explanation: The passage says that every summer the pond dried up, so the women had to fetch water from three kilometres away.

Passage: Honeybees live together in large groups called colonies. Each colony has one queen, a few hundred drones and thousands of worker bees. The queen lays eggs, while the workers do almost all the other jobs: they build the honeycomb with wax, clean the hive, guard the entrance and collect nectar from flowers. A worker bee that finds a good patch of flowers returns to the hive and performs a 'waggle dance' to tell the others where the flowers are. As bees move from flower to flower, they carry pollen, which helps plants produce fruits and seeds.

Question: Who lays the eggs in a honeybee colony?
questions.explanation: 'The queen lays eggs, while the workers do almost all the other jobs.'

Passage: On her way to school, Meena found a purse lying near the bus stop. It contained some money and the identity card of an old man named Harish Chand. Although she was getting late, Meena went to the nearby police chowki and handed over the purse. The next day, the police officer and Mr. Harish Chand visited her school. Mr. Chand said the money was meant for his wife's medicines. The principal praised Meena in the morning assembly, and her classmates clapped loudly.

Question: Where did Meena find the purse?
questions.explanation: 'Meena found a purse lying near the bus stop.'
